fact: The Civil Service Agency integrates National Identification Numbers into government employees' ID cards through the NIR portal, and Sargbe says this has helped remove ghost names from the payroll.

An MoU between the Civil Service Agency and NIR provides that civil servants' working ID cards will carry National Identification Numbers and that NBIS is used in the government employee verification headcount.
The paper's findings state the NEC and NIR databases operate as two separate databases, so the voter register is not drawn from the NIR.
The NIR and the finance ministry built an interface to audit the government payroll against the registry as new employees join, shared with the audit and civil service agencies.
The NIR says a 2018 payroll cleanup using registry attributes found only 60,000 of about 80,000 payroll names showed up.

The CSA and NIR agreed on 27 May 2024 to put National Identification Numbers on the civil-service ID cards for all 103 government spending entities and to use NIR verification to clean up the government payroll.
